LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Say what should happen if a condition becomes true.
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: 如果 or 要是 opens the condition. 就 clearly points to the result that follows.

lessonWorld.title: Prepare for a change
lessonWorld.prompt: The doctor explains what Guoan should do if the fever returns.
lessonWorld.traditional: 如果發燒了，就吃紅色的藥。
lessonWorld.simplified: 如果发烧了，就吃红色的药。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī hóngsè de yào.
lessonWorld.english: If you develop a fever, take the red medicine.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.pattern: 如果／要是 + condition， 就 + result

patternRows.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.
If you feel unwell, then see a doctor.
If he feels unwell, then he rests.

items.question: Where does 就 go in an if-then sentence?
items.answer: 就 starts the result, after the condition. It never sits inside the condition.

right.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: In the fever sentence, where does 了 go?
items.answer: 了 goes right after the action word that marks the change: 發燒了. At the very end it would change the sentence into a new decision, not a health instruction.

right.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī yào.
right.english: If you develop a fever, take medicine.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

items.question: Can I say the result first, like in English?
items.answer: No — the condition comes first, then 就 + the result: IF this, THEN that. 要是 works the same as 如果.

right.english: If you have a fever, then rest.

discoveryLab.title: Change the condition, change the result
discoveryLab.description: The left side opens a possible situation. 就 points to the response.

choices.label: Fever
choices.english: If you have a fever, take medicine.
choices.note: 發燒 is the condition; 吃藥 is the response.

choices.label: Unwell
choices.traditional: 如果不舒服，就去看醫生。
choices.simplified: 如果不舒服，就去看医生。
choices.pinyin: Rúguǒ bù shūfu, jiù qù kàn yīshēng.
choices.english: If you feel unwell, see a doctor.
choices.note: 就 makes the condition-to-result link explicit.

choices.label: Cold weather
choices.pinyin: Yàoshi tiānqì lěng, jiù dài kǒuzhào.
choices.english: If the weather is cold, wear a mask.
choices.note: 要是 works like 如果 in this pattern.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Think in two boxes: IF this becomes true → THEN do this.

ruleContrast.title: Clearer link, not a fake error
ruleContrast.description: Mandarin advice can leave out 就. The full book pattern makes the condition and result easier to see.

examples.label: Natural advice
examples.explanation: The advice is understandable without 就.

examples.label: Clear if–then link
examples.traditional: 如果不舒服，就去看醫生。
examples.simplified: 如果不舒服，就去看医生。

examples.label: 就 in the condition
examples.traditional: 如果就不舒服，去看醫生。
examples.simplified: 如果就不舒服，去看医生。
examples.explanation: Here 就 should start the result, not sit inside the condition.

examples.teachingNote: A decision depends on another person.

text.traditional: 要是他不去，我們就不要去了。
text.simplified: 要是他不去，我们就不要去了。
text.pinyin: Yàoshi tā bú qù, wǒmen jiù bú yào qù le.
text.english: If he does not go, then we will not go.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

examples.teachingNote: The result gives friendly permission.

text.traditional: 如果你想吃，就多吃一點吧！
text.simplified: 如果你想吃，就多吃一点吧！
text.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ xiǎng chī, jiù duō chī yìdiǎn ba!
text.english: If you want to eat, have a little more!

examples.teachingNote: A future plan changes with the condition.

text.traditional: 如果明天天氣不好，我們就不要去游泳了。
text.simplified: 如果明天天气不好，我们就不要去游泳了。
text.pinyin: Rúguǒ míngtiān tiānqì bù hǎo, wǒmen jiù bú yào qù yóuyǒng le.
text.english: If the weather is bad tomorrow, we will not go swimming.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

examples.teachingNote: Source clinic instruction.

text.traditional: 要是發燒了，就吃紅色的藥。
text.simplified: 要是发烧了，就吃红色的药。
text.pinyin: Yàoshi fāshāo le, jiù chī hóngsè de yào.
text.english: If you develop a fever, take the red medicine.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

The result needs an action.

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleEnglish: Use 會 for an Expected Future
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Say what you expect will happen.
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: With a future time, 會 introduces the action you expect. Put the time before 會.

lessonWorld.title: Promise a visit
lessonWorld.prompt: Yuanzhen tells Guoan what she plans to do tomorrow.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我明天會帶水果去看你。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我明天会带水果去看你。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì dài shuǐguǒ qù kàn nǐ.
lessonWorld.english: I will bring fruit to visit you tomorrow.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

patternRows.english: I will come tomorrow.
The doctor will speak tomorrow.
He will go to the hospital tomorrow.

items.question: I will come tomorrow — where does 明天 go?
items.answer: Before 會. Time first, then 會 + the action: 我明天會來。

items.question: Does 會 mean “can” or “will”?
items.answer: With no time word, 會 can read as a skill: 我會說中文 is “I can speak Chinese”. Add a time word and it reads as “will”.

right.english: I will go to the hospital tomorrow.

items.question: For “I will visit you tomorrow”, can I use 可以?
items.answer: 可以 says you are allowed or able. For something you expect to happen, use 會.

right.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kàn nǐ.

discoveryLab.title: Let the time choose the meaning
discoveryLab.description: 會 can describe ability or an expected future. Look for the time clue.

choices.label: Ability
choices.note: No future time here; 會 means a learned skill.

choices.label: Tomorrow
choices.note: 明天 makes this an expected future.

choices.label: Visit Guoan
choices.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kàn Guó’ān.
choices.note: Time first, then 會 + action.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 我會明天去 → 我明天會去
choices.simplified: 我会明天去 → 我明天会去
choices.pinyin: wǒ huì míngtiān qù → wǒ míngtiān huì qù
choices.note: The future time frames the whole action.

discoveryLab.takeaway: A future time before 會 helps the listener read it as “will.”

examples.teachingNote: Today frames the expected action.

text.traditional: 我今天會去百貨公司幫你買。
text.simplified: 我今天会去百货公司帮你买。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān huì qù bǎihuògōngsī bāng nǐ mǎi.
text.english: I will go to the department store and buy it for you today.

examples.teachingNote: Ask about an expected future.

text.traditional: 國安明天會來學校考試嗎？
text.simplified: 国安明天会来学校考试吗？
text.pinyin: Guó’ān míngtiān huì lái xuéxiào kǎoshì ma?
text.english: Will Guoan come to school for the exam tomorrow?

examples.teachingNote: Source prediction in the clinic.

text.traditional: 醫生會給你三天的藥。
text.simplified: 医生会给你三天的药。
text.pinyin: Yīshēng huì gěi nǐ sān tiān de yào.
text.english: The doctor will give you three days of medicine.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

examples.teachingNote: The care plan from Dialogue 1.

text.traditional: 我明天會帶水果去看他。
text.simplified: 我明天会带水果去看他。
text.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì dài shuǐguǒ qù kàn tā.
text.english: I will bring fruit to visit him tomorrow.

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.exercisePreview: Put the time before 會 and the action after it.

questions.correctFeedback: 會 comes before the expected action.
The expected action follows 會.
會 starts the full future action.

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.titleEnglish: Connect a Person to an Action with 跟
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Use 跟 to do things together with someone, to speak or request from someone, and to learn or borrow from someone.
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: 跟 connects you with another person. Use it to do things together (“with”), to talk or ask (“to”), or to learn or borrow (“from”).

lessonWorld.title: Send the right care message
lessonWorld.prompt: Yuanzhen needs to pass the teacher’s advice to Guoan.
lessonWorld.traditional: 老師要我跟國安說幾句話。
lessonWorld.simplified: 老师要我跟国安说几句话。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Lǎoshī yào wǒ gēn Guó’ān shuō jǐ jù huà.
lessonWorld.english: The teacher wants me to say a few things to Guoan.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.pattern: 和…一起 ｜ 對…說話／請假 ｜ 向…學習／借

patternRows.english: Tonight I will eat with a friend.
He speaks English with his family.
I learn calligraphy from Teacher Li.

items.question: I go to the hospital with my friend — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: Right before the person who joins you: 跟朋友. The person never comes before 跟.

right.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.

items.question: I tell my friend something — where does my friend go?
items.answer: The person you tell comes right after 跟, before the action word: 我跟朋友說。

items.question: Can 和 do the same job as 跟?
items.answer: 和 lists two people as equals — “my friend and I”. 跟 connects the person to your action: go WITH, speak TO.

right.english: I speak Chinese with the doctor.

discoveryLab.title: Move 跟, move the connection
discoveryLab.description: The same people can join different parts of the event.

choices.label: Go together
choices.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.
choices.note: 跟朋友 goes with 去醫院: the friend joins the trip.

choices.label: Talk there
choices.pinyin: Wǒ qù yīyuàn gēn péngyǒu shuōhuà.
choices.english: I go to the hospital to speak with my friend.
choices.note: Here 跟朋友 goes with 說話, not the trip.

choices.label: Tell the teacher
choices.english: I first ask the teacher for leave.
choices.note: 老師 receives the request.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Read 跟 with the person and the action after it.

text.traditional: 今天晚上我要跟朋友吃飯。
text.simplified: 今天晚上我要跟朋友吃饭。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒ yào gēn péngyǒu chīfàn.
text.english: Tonight I am going to eat dinner with a friend.

text.traditional: 我常常跟他一起去百貨公司買東西。
text.simplified: 我常常跟他一起去百货公司买东西。
text.pinyin: Wǒ chángcháng gēn tā yìqǐ qù bǎihuò gōngsī mǎi dōngxi.
text.english: I often go to the department store together with him to buy things.

text.traditional: 我喜歡跟家人去海邊玩。
text.simplified: 我喜欢跟家人去海边玩。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān gēn jiārén qù hǎibiān wán.
text.english: I like going to the beach with my family.

text.traditional: 他跟家人說英文，跟同學說中文。
text.simplified: 他跟家人说英文，跟同学说中文。
text.pinyin: Tā gēn jiārén shuō Yīngwén, gēn tóngxué shuō Zhōngwén.
text.english: He speaks English to his family and Chinese to his classmates.

text.traditional: 計程車司機跟我說：「去機場 1,200 塊錢。」
text.simplified: 计程车司机跟我说：「去机场 1,200 块钱。」
text.pinyin: Jìchéngchē sījī gēn wǒ shuō: "Qù jīchǎng 1,200 kuài qián."
text.english: The taxi driver said to me: "Going to the airport is 1,200 dollars."

text.traditional: 我明天不能來上課，今天要先跟老師請假。
text.simplified: 我明天不能来上课，今天要先跟老师请假。
text.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān bù néng lái shàngkè, jīntiān yào xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià.
text.english: I cannot attend class tomorrow, so today I need to ask the teacher for leave first.

words.pinyin: wǒ míngtiān bù néng lái shàngkè
words.meaning: I cannot come to class tomorrow

examples.teachingNote: 跟...學 means to learn from someone.

text.traditional: 我跟沈老師學書法。
text.simplified: 我跟沈老师学书法。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn Shěn lǎoshī xué shūfǎ.
text.english: I learn calligraphy from Teacher Shen.

examples.teachingNote: 跟...要錢 means to ask for money from parents.

text.traditional: 他二十歲了，不跟爸媽要錢了。
text.simplified: 他二十岁了，不跟爸妈要钱了。
text.pinyin: Tā èrshí suì le, bù gēn bàmā yào qián le.
text.english: He is twenty years old; he no longer asks his parents for money.

examples.teachingNote: 跟...買舊車 means to buy a used car from a friend.

text.traditional: 我不想跟朋友買舊車，我想買新車。
text.simplified: 我不想跟朋友买旧车，我想买新车。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng gēn péngyǒu mǎi jiù chē, wǒ xiǎng mǎi xīn chē.
text.english: I don't want to buy a used car from a friend; I want to buy a new car.

跟他一起 highlights the joint action.

segments.traditional: 我明天不能來上課，今天要先

questions.correctFeedback: 跟老師請假 is the canonical expression for requesting absence from a teacher.

tiles.meaning: looks at calligraphy at Teacher Li

subsections.title: Doing Things with Someone (With)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you do an activity with, like “have dinner with friends” or “go shopping with him.”

patternRows.english: Tonight I will eat with a friend.

subsections.title: Talking to Someone (To)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you are talking to, like “he speaks English to his family” or “asking the teacher for time off.”

patternRows.english: He speaks English with his family.

subsections.title: Learning or Getting from Someone (From)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you learn or receive something from, like “learn calligraphy from Teacher Shen” or “borrow money from a friend.”

patternRows.english: I learn calligraphy from Teacher Li.

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleTraditional: 把行動調多一點或少一點
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleEnglish: Do an Action More or Less
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Give useful advice with 多 or 少 before an action.
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: Put 多 or 少 before the action you want someone to increase or reduce.

lessonWorld.title: Adjust the advice
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan needs more water and rest, but less phone time.
lessonWorld.traditional: 你應該多喝水、少看手機。
lessonWorld.simplified: 你应该多喝水、少看手机。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō hē shuǐ, shǎo kàn shǒujī.
lessonWorld.english: You should drink more water and look at your phone less.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

patternRows.english: drink more water
rest more
look at the phone less

items.question: Why can’t I just say 多水 for “more water”?
items.answer: 多 and 少 adjust an action word. Water is a thing, so add the action first: 多喝水。

items.question: Does 多 come before or after the action?
items.answer: Before it: 多休息, 少看手機. Never after the action word.

items.question: How do I say “drink MORE water” as advice?
items.answer: 很多水 means “a lot of water”. For advice to drink more, put 多 right before the action: 多喝水。

discoveryLab.title: Turn the action up or down
discoveryLab.description: 多 and 少 change how often or how much the action happens.

choices.label: More water
choices.note: 多 sits before the action 喝.

choices.label: More rest
choices.note: The advice increases the action.

choices.label: Less phone
choices.note: 少 reduces 看手機.

choices.label: Repair the advice
choices.note: Water is a thing. Health advice needs the action 喝.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Choose an action first. Put 多 or 少 directly before it.

examples.teachingNote: One action goes up, one goes down.

text.traditional: 你應該多運動，少喝一點兒酒。
text.simplified: 你应该多运动，少喝一点儿酒。
text.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō yùndòng, shǎo hē yìdiǎnr jiǔ.
text.english: You should exercise more and drink a little less alcohol.

examples.teachingNote: Source health advice.

text.traditional: 我發燒了，醫生跟我說要多喝水、多休息、少看手機。
text.simplified: 我发烧了，医生跟我说要多喝水、多休息、少看手机。
text.pinyin: Wǒ fāshāo le, yīshēng gēn wǒ shuō yào duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxi, shǎo kàn shǒujī.
text.english: I have a fever; the doctor told me to drink more water, rest more, and look at my phone less.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

examples.teachingNote: 多 changes 休息.

text.traditional: 生病的時候要多休息。
text.simplified: 生病的时候要多休息。
text.pinyin: Shēngbìng de shíhou yào duō xiūxi.
text.english: When sick, rest more.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

examples.teachingNote: The pattern can repeat across several actions.

text.traditional: 我們學習語言，平常應該要多聽、多說、多寫、多練習。
text.simplified: 我们学习语言，平常应该要多听、多说、多写、多练习。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxí yǔyán, píngcháng yīnggāi yào duō tīng, duō shuō, duō xiě, duō liànxí.
text.english: When we learn a language, we should listen, speak, write, and practice more in daily life.

questions.correctFeedback: The advice includes the action 喝.

segments.hint: Put the adjustment before the action.

questions.correctFeedback: 多 comes before 休息.
questions.repairFeedback: Put the adjustment before the action.

LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleEnglish: Noun Modified by a Clause with 的
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: Identify a person or thing by describing it first.
LESSON_TEN_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: Put your description first, add 的, and then say the person or thing you mean: Description + 的 + Noun. If you want to point out someone specific, add “this” or “that” right after 的.

lessonWorld.title: Find the person who needs help
lessonWorld.prompt: Several people are waiting. Which person has a cold?
lessonWorld.english: Find the person who has a cold.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

patternRows.english: The characters I wrote.
The person who has a cold.
That doctor wearing a mask.

items.question: The person who has a cold — which word comes last?
items.answer: The person. Put the description first, then 的, then the person: 感冒的人。

right.english: the person who has a cold

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

items.question: Do I always need 的 between the description and the person?
items.answer: Yes. 的 is the link: description + 的 + person. Without it, the words do not join into one label.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

items.question: The medicine the doctor gave — where does 的 go?
items.answer: Right after the action word, before the thing: 醫生給的藥。The whole description stays before 的.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

discoveryLab.title: Change the label, find someone new
discoveryLab.description: The noun stays last. Everything before 的 tells you which one.

choices.label: Has a cold
choices.english: the person who has a cold
choices.note: 感冒 identifies the person.

choices.label: Wears a mask
choices.note: The whole action 戴口罩 identifies the person.

choices.label: Mask-wearing doctor
choices.note: Changing the final noun changes who the label identifies.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 人感冒的 → 感冒的人
choices.simplified: 人感冒的 → 感冒的人
choices.pinyin: rén gǎnmào de → gǎnmào de rén
choices.english: Move the description before 的 and the noun.
choices.note: Chinese builds the label first, then names the noun.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask: “Which person or thing?” Put the answer before 的.

examples.teachingNote: The modifying clause 我寫 precedes the modified noun 字.

text.traditional: 我寫的字太小了，老師看不懂。
text.simplified: 我写的字太小了，老师看不懂。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiě de zì tài xiǎo le, lǎoshī kànbudǒng.
text.english: The characters I wrote are too small; the teacher cannot read them.

examples.teachingNote: 他唱 modifies the noun 歌.

text.traditional: 他唱的歌很好聽，是哪國歌？
text.simplified: 他唱的歌很好听，是哪国歌？
text.pinyin: Tā chàng de gē hěn hǎotīng, shì nǎ guó gē?
text.english: The song he sings sounds very nice; which country's song is it?

examples.teachingNote: 他們說 modifies the noun 話.

text.traditional: 我不懂他們說的話，你懂嗎？
text.simplified: 我不懂他们说的话，你懂吗？
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù dǒng tāmen shuō de huà, nǐ dǒng ma?
text.english: I don't understand the words they are saying; do you understand?

examples.teachingNote: 在台北坐捷運 modifies 人 as a category of people.

text.traditional: 在台北坐捷運的人很多。
text.simplified: 在台北坐捷运的人很多。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiběi zuò jiéyùn de rén hěn duō.
text.english: People who take the MRT in Taipei are many.

examples.teachingNote: 會說中文 modifies 人.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Connect a Person to an Action with 跟
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 跟 to do things together with someone, to speak or request from someone, and to learn or borrow from someone.
grammarPages.explanation: 跟 connects you with another person. Use it to do things together (“with”), to talk or ask (“to”), or to learn or borrow (“from”).

items.question: I go to the hospital with my friend — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: Right before the person who joins you: 跟朋友. The person never comes before 跟.

right.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.

items.question: I tell my friend something — where does my friend go?
items.answer: The person you tell comes right after 跟, before the action word: 我跟朋友說。

items.question: Can 和 do the same job as 跟?
items.answer: 和 lists two people as equals — “my friend and I”. 跟 connects the person to your action: go WITH, speak TO.

right.english: I speak Chinese with the doctor.

items.question: Why can’t I just say 多水 for “more water”?
items.answer: 多 and 少 adjust an action word. Water is a thing, so add the action first: 多喝水。

items.question: Does 多 come before or after the action?
items.answer: Before it: 多休息, 少看手機. Never after the action word.

items.question: How do I say “drink MORE water” as advice?
items.answer: 很多水 means “a lot of water”. For advice to drink more, put 多 right before the action: 多喝水。

discoveryLab.title: Turn the action up or down
discoveryLab.description: 多 and 少 change how often or how much the action happens.

choices.label: More water
choices.note: 多 sits before the action 喝.

choices.label: More rest
choices.note: The advice increases the action.

choices.label: Less phone
choices.note: 少 reduces 看手機.

choices.label: Repair the advice
choices.note: Water is a thing. Health advice needs the action 喝.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Choose an action first. Put 多 or 少 directly before it.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 會 for an Expected Future
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what you expect will happen.
grammarPages.explanation: With a future time, 會 introduces the action you expect. Put the time before 會.

lessonWorld.title: Promise a visit
lessonWorld.prompt: Yuanzhen tells Guoan what she plans to do tomorrow.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我明天會帶水果去看你。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我明天会带水果去看你。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì dài shuǐguǒ qù kàn nǐ.
lessonWorld.english: I will bring fruit to visit you tomorrow.

patternRows.english: I will come tomorrow.
The doctor will speak tomorrow.
He will go to the hospital tomorrow.

items.question: I will come tomorrow — where does 明天 go?
items.answer: Before 會. Time first, then 會 + the action: 我明天會來。

items.question: Does 會 mean “can” or “will”?
items.answer: With no time word, 會 can read as a skill: 我會說中文 is “I can speak Chinese”. Add a time word and it reads as “will”.

right.english: I will go to the hospital tomorrow.

items.question: For “I will visit you tomorrow”, can I use 可以?
items.answer: 可以 says you are allowed or able. For something you expect to happen, use 會.

right.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kàn nǐ.

discoveryLab.title: Let the time choose the meaning
discoveryLab.description: 會 can describe ability or an expected future. Look for the time clue.

choices.label: Ability
choices.note: No future time here; 會 means a learned skill.

choices.label: Tomorrow
choices.note: 明天 makes this an expected future.

choices.label: Visit Guoan
choices.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kàn Guó’ān.
choices.note: Time first, then 會 + action.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 我會明天去 → 我明天會去
choices.simplified: 我会明天去 → 我明天会去
choices.pinyin: wǒ huì míngtiān qù → wǒ míngtiān huì qù
choices.note: The future time frames the whole action.

discoveryLab.takeaway: A future time before 會 helps the listener read it as “will.”

examples.teachingNote: Today frames the expected action.

text.traditional: 我今天會去百貨公司幫你買。
text.simplified: 我今天会去百货公司帮你买。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān huì qù bǎihuògōngsī bāng nǐ mǎi.
text.english: I will go to the department store and buy it for you today.

examples.teachingNote: Ask about an expected future.

text.traditional: 國安明天會來學校考試嗎？
text.simplified: 国安明天会来学校考试吗？
text.pinyin: Guó’ān míngtiān huì lái xuéxiào kǎoshì ma?
text.english: Will Guoan come to school for the exam tomorrow?

text.pinyin: Yīshēng huì gěi nǐ sān tiān de yào.

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what should happen if a condition becomes true.
grammarPages.explanation: 如果 or 要是 opens the condition. 就 clearly points to the result that follows.

lessonWorld.title: Prepare for a change
lessonWorld.prompt: The doctor explains what Guoan should do if the fever returns.
lessonWorld.traditional: 如果發燒了，就吃紅色的藥。
lessonWorld.simplified: 如果发烧了，就吃红色的药。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī hóngsè de yào.
lessonWorld.english: If you develop a fever, take the red medicine.

grammarPages.pattern: 如果／要是 + condition， 就 + result

patternRows.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.
If you feel unwell, then see a doctor.
If he feels unwell, then he rests.

items.question: Where does 就 go in an if-then sentence?
items.answer: 就 starts the result, after the condition. It never sits inside the condition.

right.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: In the fever sentence, where does 了 go?
items.answer: 了 goes right after the action word that marks the change: 發燒了. At the very end it would change the sentence into a new decision, not a health instruction.

right.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī yào.
right.english: If you develop a fever, take medicine.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

items.question: Can I say the result first, like in English?
items.answer: No — the condition comes first, then 就 + the result: IF this, THEN that. 要是 works the same as 如果.

right.english: If you have a fever, then rest.

discoveryLab.title: Change the condition, change the result
discoveryLab.description: The left side opens a possible situation. 就 points to the response.

choices.label: Fever
choices.english: If you have a fever, take medicine.
choices.note: 發燒 is the condition; 吃藥 is the response.

choices.label: Unwell
choices.traditional: 如果不舒服，就去看醫生。
choices.simplified: 如果不舒服，就去看医生。
choices.pinyin: Rúguǒ bù shūfu, jiù qù kàn yīshēng.
choices.english: If you feel unwell, see a doctor.
choices.note: 就 makes the condition-to-result link explicit.

choices.label: Cold weather
choices.pinyin: Yàoshi tiānqì lěng, jiù dài kǒuzhào.
choices.english: If the weather is cold, wear a mask.
choices.note: 要是 works like 如果 in this pattern.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Think in two boxes: IF this becomes true → THEN do this.

ruleContrast.title: Clearer link, not a fake error
ruleContrast.description: Mandarin advice can leave out 就. The full book pattern makes the condition and result easier to see.

examples.label: Natural advice
examples.explanation: The advice is understandable without 就.

examples.label: Clear if–then link
examples.traditional: 如果不舒服，就去看醫生。
examples.simplified: 如果不舒服，就去看医生。

examples.label: 就 in the condition

examples.simplified: 如果就不舒服，去看医生。
examples.explanation: Here 就 should start the result, not sit inside the condition.
